caption:
Reuters reports that Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, citing two people familiar with the matter.
That makes three alleged affairs. He has admitted one. Nvidia declined to comment.
The report landed the same day he resigned as CEO.

Is there more coming?

paragraphs.text: Jensen Huang had an affair with a current Nvidia employee that had not previously been made public, Reuters reported on Thursday, November 12, 2026, according to accounts of the report by TechCrunch and Forbes. The report came on the same day Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia and left its board.

Reuters is withholding the employee's name, TechCrunch wrote. Neither TechCrunch nor Forbes gives her role at the company, and neither describes how many people Reuters spoke to. Forbes described her as a second Nvidia employee linked to Huang.
Jensen Huang's third alleged affair: what is known

The new report brings the number of alleged affairs to three. The first, and the one at the center of the scandal, involved a woman whom Forbes describes as a suspected Chinese spy. The second, according to earlier reports cited by both outlets, involved an Nvidia executive. The third is the employee in the Reuters report.

Huang has formally acknowledged only one of the three, according to Forbes. Neither article includes a statement from Huang or from Nvidia about the Reuters report, so the new account stands as a report by one news agency and has not been confirmed or denied by the people involved.
The report followed his resignation by hours

Huang stepped down as CEO and as a board member earlier on November 12, 2026, TechCrunch reported. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, and no permanent successor has been named. Forbes wrote that the accusations and reports about the affairs fueled the resignation; Nvidia itself has not given a reason.

The scrutiny is not limited to the company. TechCrunch reported that Huang has been called to testify before Congress about the national security implications of the first relationship, with a hearing expected in the coming weeks. No date has been given.
What is alleged and what is confirmed

Confirmed: Huang is no longer Nvidia's CEO or a director, and Kress is running the company on an interim basis. Acknowledged by Huang: one affair, according to Forbes. Reported but not confirmed by him or by Nvidia: the relationship with an executive and the relationship in the new Reuters report.

NeuraFeed's reading: the timing matters more than the count. A report that surfaces after a resignation suggests the story is not finished. For Nvidia, each new account involving an employee moves the issue further from one person's private conduct and closer to questions about workplace rules and what directors were told. For an interim CEO, that is a harder situation to steady than a single departure.
Watch for a response from Huang or Nvidia to the Reuters report, for the date of the congressional hearing, and for whether the board says what it knew before it accepted his resignation.
